subject: SolisHealth: Increased token latency & errors — possible KV cache starvation
messages:

Cc: procurement@solishealth.com
Date: Tue, 9 Apr 2029 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Increased latency & 5xxs from your hosted API (SolisHealth production)

Ben —

We started seeing a sudden jump in p95 latency and a rise in 5xx rates across our key inference routes (document-summarize and patient-qna) around 14:42 PDT today. A few notes: 

- Scope: all requests from the "sh-sv-1" pool (region us-west).
- Impact: p95 increased from ~220ms to ~1.4s; error rate to 1.8% (previously ~0.05%).
- Business impact: blocking several scheduled batch jobs and delaying internal clinical workflows.

We attached a sampling of failed requests and client-side timings (solis_health_errors_20290409.zip). Can you confirm whether this is an ongoing capacity/serving problem on your side? We need an update and an ETA for mitigation within the next 90 minutes — our Ops and procurement teams are on standby.

If helpful, we can open a bridge. Please advise next steps.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
SolisHealth — Senior Platform Ops
A: aisha.khan@solishealth.com

Immediate plan:
- Marissa will validate whether we have HOL (head-of-line) blocking or cache-eviction churn on the Solis tenant.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@solishealth.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Apr 2029 15:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Increased latency & 5xxs from your hosted API (SolisHealth production)

Hi Ben / Aisha — quick update from the runtime side after an initial triage of the Solis tenant pool:

Summary of findings (first-pass):
- We are seeing KV cache churn and priority-queue lane starvation for the "sh-sv-1" pool beginning ~14:40 PDT.
- The majority of hot prefixes are extremely skewed; small set of prefixes is being evicted and reloaded repeatedly causing HOL for subsequent requests.
- Observed concurrent batch lanes hitting the same prefix, leading to inflight KV lock contention and bursts of 429/5xx when prefetch fails and fallback kicks in.

Immediate mitigations we can apply with minimal disruption:
1) Temporarily reduce max_batch_size for the affected model routes to 8 (current 32) for sh-sv-1. Command (ops):
   -- apply-config --pool sh-sv-1 --route document-summarize --set max_batch_size=8
2) Increase per-tenant KV cache occupancy to reserve ~20% extra for Solis (pin top prefixes):
   -- cache-adjust --tenant solishealth --reserve 20% --pin-prefixes top:200
3) Adjust eviction policy from pure LRU to LRU+TTL (short TTL=10m) for noisy prefixes to reduce eviction/reload cycles:
   -- cache-policy --tenant solishealth --policy lru_ttl --ttl 10m
4) Enable a short prefetch backoff window (60s) to avoid thundering re-prefetch for newly-evicted keys.

Operational notes:
- These changes are low risk and reversible. We expect latency to drop within 5–10 minutes after applying (p95 improvement). Error rate should follow as prefetch contention subsides.
- If those mitigations do not stabilize within 30 minutes, we will schedule a rolling restart of the affected shard group during a 10-minute planned maintenance window (we will coordinate exact times).

Attachments: I pushed a KV snapshot (kv_snapshot_20290409.txt) to the ticket with eviction histograms and prefix frequency.

Aisha — can you confirm whether your client side can tolerate a temporary reduced batch size? That helps us decide the order of mitigations.

Marissa Cole
Lead, Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Exec-Oncall <exec_oncall@redwood.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive summary: SolisHealth KV eviction/starvation incident + customer request for remediation credit

Executive team —

After the incident on 2029-04-09 impacting SolisHealth (SL-7843), runtime telemetry shows the root cause as high-frequency eviction/reload cycles on their tenant's hot prefixes combined with default batching settings that amplified HOL blocking. Marissa applied targeted mitigations (batch reduction, reserve cache, LRU+TTL) which stabilized p95 to pre-incident levels within ~12 minutes.

Customer ask: SolisOps has requested a short credit for the SLA window (they were blocked for ~22 minutes at high severity). They also asked for a short retro and confirmation of long-term fixes (we proposed prefix pinning automation and tenant-aware batch tuning).

Recommendation: approve a goodwill credit for the impacted 30-minute window and prioritize automation ticket (OPS-1329) to detect heavy eviction churn and auto-apply the cache-reserve/pinning rule.

I am available to brief on the technical remediation steps and timeline.

Jonas Weber
Director, Capacity Planning — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
